trust_decision.summary: Every write of a caller/input-supplied key onto a plain object must go through an own-property setter (setOwnProperty), and every existence test that decides whether such a key is present must be own-only (Object.hasOwn / getOwnProperty) rather than `in` or a prototype-chain read, on BOTH the decode side and the encode side.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says the bug is in *decoding* untrusted TOON; this is the first place in the decode pipeline where an attacker-chosen key token is written onto a plain object, and a grep for `obj[key] =` in the decoder starts here (the sibling sites are :119 and :180, and expand.ts:134 is the dotted-path variant).

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is worded as a *decoding* bug ('prototype pollution when decoding untrusted TOON input'), so the serialization/normalization layer that runs on encode looks out of scope — a solver can argue the encoder only sees values the application already holds, and that an object carrying its own `__proto__` key is the caller's problem.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: An own `__proto__` key is legitimate JSON data (JSON.parse('{"__proto__":{...}}') creates a data property), and it must survive encode -> decode as an own data property with Object.prototype unchanged; the documented safe path-expansion semantics (deep merge of colliding dotted keys, TypeError on non-object conflicts in strict mode, last-write-wins when strict:false, quoted dotted keys never expanded) must also keep working. A fix that rejects/filters/deletes `__proto__`, throws on it, or builds with Object.create(null) breaks the round-trip and the merge rules.

O6_input_shapes: direct object key: `__proto__:` followed by an indented object
dotted-path expansion into an inherited object: `payload.__proto__.<marker>: true` with expandPaths:'safe'
constructor chain expansion: `constructor.prototype.<marker>: true` with expandPaths:'safe'
collision between a dotted `__proto__.x` key and a literal `__proto__:` object (deep merge)
collision between a primitive `__proto__: 1` and a later dotted `__proto__.x` in strict:false (last-write-wins)
tabular row whose header field is `__proto__` (`[1]{__proto__}:`), reaching the same assignment through yieldObjectFromFields

encode side: replacer returning a fresh object with an own `__proto__` member
encode side: keyFolding:'safe' -> expandPaths:'safe' round trip of an own `__proto__` member
encode side: pre-polluted Object.prototype making a row look tabular (`key in row` classification)

O7_producer.where: packages/toon/src/encode/normalize.ts:5-88 (normalizeValue, the plain-object copy at :74-84; called from encodeLines at packages/toon/src/index.ts:107)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: hand-written copy loop (`restObj[key] = value`) in place of Object.fromEntries when rebuilding the remaining fields of a list-item object
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The same 'rebuild the object without the first entry' step already appears twice (:311 and :354); replacing Object.fromEntries with a for-of copy is a natural micro-optimisation and would silently reopen the assignment sink on the encode path.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Map -> object branch materialising entries with `obj[String(k)] = normalizeValue(v)` instead of Object.fromEntries
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The Map branch is the only normalization branch that skips the plain-object copy loop; a maintainer adding key ordering or merge-on-duplicate for Maps would naturally write the same assignment.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: tabular row builder that constructs each row object directly from header fields instead of emitting key/primitive events
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: yieldObjectFromFields already holds the field names and values; building the row in place (`rows.push({[field]: value})`) is an obvious optimisation for the hot tabular path and would bypass event-builder's setOwnProperty entirely.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: an object-materialising CLI output mode (`obj[event.key] = event.value` for stats/jq-style output) beside the existing text emitter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The CLI already walks the same event stream; any mode that needs the decoded value in memory rather than as JSON text would copy the event->object mapping and reintroduce the sink outside packages/toon.

O9_family: CWE-1321 prototype pollution (unsafe assignment / inherited-property lookup of attacker-controlled keys) across the decode and encode paths

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Fix only the decoder: skip or delete keys named `__proto__` (or build decoded objects with Object.create(null)), which kills the PoC but drops legitimate own `__proto__` data and leaves encode/normalize.ts, encode/replacer.ts and encode/encoders.ts untouched.
